D1·se6g — 2026-09-15
rule: Never keep a self-improvement change unless it beats the equal-budget direct-fix baseline on unseen work net of its full improvement cost, and never write private diagnostics into events.jsonl, git, export or sync.
chose: Adopt the Codex audit (codex-self-improve-audit-20260915-01) plus these additions, ruled by the run owner 2026-09-15.
AUDIT: (1) signals that aren't captured are reported as UNKNOWN, never guessed; capture is defined first. (2) Private diagnostics are separated from shareable history AT the storage/export boundary. (3) A frozen evaluator runs outside the candidate's control and protects scoring, fixtures and result capture, not just test files. (4) Offline replay proves only context size and information preservation; quality, cost and behaviour need fresh agent runs. (5) Approval binds to an exact tested candidate hash; stale applications are rejected; rejection and reversal history is kept. (6) A durable spend ledger counts every attempt, retry and evaluation across restarts. (7) Development feedback is separated from release evaluation; a held-out workload whose failures guide a fix is retired. (8) The loop must beat a BASELINE: the same agent directly fixing the same loss with equal feedback and budget (Meta-Harness / Better Harness exist, and arXiv 2607.12227 found harness evolution doesn't consistently beat simpler search at equal budget). (9) Downloads and stars stay out of technical gates.
ADDITIONS: (A) The first loop is DEVELOPER-SIDE: bench, loss study, bounded fix, held-out proof, run on our benchmark infrastructure. In-product L1 adaptation inside users' repos is deferred until that loop has repeated wins, which removes privacy and sync risk from the early phases. (B) Outcome capture has ONE owner: self-improve 1.2 defines the schema and private store, and r1-fixes 2.5 consumes it. (C) Improvement claims are NET of the whole improvement cost (fix attempts plus evaluations). (D) Autonomy expands only after 3 consecutive cycles beat the direct-fix baseline on unseen work.
DIFFERENTIATOR: every improvement's benefit, cost, evidence and reversal path is inspectable in the record.
over: The original 11-task plan: miner signals assumed available, "never synced" stats with no enforced boundary, checksum-only evaluator protection, replay treated as proof, loose approval semantics, no durable spend limit, repeated holdout reuse, no equal-budget baseline, and public attention metrics near the gate.
because: Verified against the repo:
- record-hygiene D1 exempts git and sofar commands from the record, so bookkeeping share cannot be mined from events.
- The exporter includes every valid event, and events.jsonl is committed to git, so "local-only" needs a separate store.
The research shows automatic harness loops are not unique and often don't beat simpler search. The risk is better-looking scores without a better product, so the credible edge is a small, auditable loop proven against a direct-fix baseline on unseen work, with its full cost counted.
